title: The History of Diablo | From Tristram To Lord of Hatred | Gaming History
description: The full history of Blizzard's Diablo series: Condor and Blizzard North, Diablo two, the record launch of Diablo three, Immortal, Diablo four and the Lord of Hatred expansion in 2026.

sections.heading: Welcome to Sanctuary
sections.script: Click, click, click, loot. Few games are as addictive as Diablo, the series that defined the action role playing game. Since the nineties, players have been descending into dark dungeons, fighting demons and chasing better and better gear. In this video we cover the complete history of Diablo: the small studio called Condor, the first game that changed from turn based to real time, the legendary Diablo two, the record breaking launch of Diablo three, the mobile experiment, and the return of the dark with Diablo four and its expansions, including Lord of Hatred in twenty twenty six. Grab your sword, your staff or your bow, and be careful, because evil has a way of finding you.

sections.heading: Condor and Blizzard North
sections.script: The story starts in nineteen ninety three with a small studio named Condor, founded by David Brevik and the brothers Erich and Max Schaefer, who met while working at a clip art company. They pitched a game with randomly generated dungeons, like old text based adventures, but with updated visuals. Blizzard, then best known for its strategy games, became involved, and in nineteen ninety six it bought the studio and renamed it Blizzard North. The design changed under Blizzard's influence. The game was originally turn based, but it became real time, gained multiplayer through Blizzard's new Battle dot net service, and dropped permanent death. That mix of fast combat and online friends turned out to be a perfect recipe, even if nobody knew it yet.

sections.heading: The first Diablo
sections.script: Diablo went on sale as nineteen ninety six turned into nineteen ninety seven. You played a lone hero who descends into the dungeon below the town of Tristram, and fought your way down level after level until you faced the Lord of Terror himself. The game had three classes, the Warrior, the Rogue and the Sorcerer, dark music that people still remember and a loot system that made every kill feel like a lottery. Because the dungeons were randomly generated, every run was different. Battle dot net allowed friends and strangers to play together. The success was huge, and Diablo became one of the most influential computer role playing games of its time, starting a whole genre of copycats.

sections.heading: Diablo II
sections.script: Diablo two was released in June two thousand, made again by Blizzard North. It added five classes, bigger towns, four acts, a skill tree and a brilliant item system with magic, rare, set and unique gear. It also improved Battle dot net so much that players around the world could trade items and join games. Blizzard said it sold more than two million seven hundred fifty thousand copies in the year two thousand, based on figures from the market tracker PC Data, calling it the fastest selling game in its history. An expansion, Lord of Destruction, followed in June two thousand one, adding two more classes and a fifth act. Even after decades, many fans still believe that Diablo two is the best action role playing game ever made.

sections.heading: The long road to number three
sections.script: After Diablo two, Blizzard North started working on a third game in two thousand one, but the story of that project was troubled. Around two thousand three, the founders left the company after a dispute with the parent company, and in two thousand five Blizzard closed Blizzard North and moved the work to its main offices. The team restarted from scratch with a new look and new ideas, and Blizzard announced Diablo three in June two thousand eight. Some fans were upset at the brighter art style and the decision to require an online connection, but the team held its course. It was a long wait, almost twelve years since the last chapter, and it became one of the most anticipated releases in computer gaming at the time.

sections.heading: Diablo III breaks records
sections.script: Diablo three launched on May fifteenth, twenty twelve. Blizzard reported that it sold more than three and a half million copies in the first twenty four hours, not counting about one point two million players who got it through a World of Warcraft promotion, and over six point three million in the first week, making it the fastest selling computer game at that time. The launch was rocky, however. Servers struggled and many players were locked out for hours, and the chief executive apologised. The game also faced criticism for its auction house, which Blizzard later removed. In March twenty fourteen, an expansion called Reaper of Souls added the Crusader class and a better loot system, and fans finally embraced the game. Today, many people consider Diablo three a great game that took a while to get going.

sections.heading: Resurrected and Immortal
sections.script: In twenty twenty one, Blizzard released Diablo two Resurrected on September twenty third, a remaster made with Vicarious Visions. It rebuilt the graphics in three dimensions but let you switch to the classic look with one button. The game launched on computers and consoles together. In June twenty twenty two came Diablo Immortal, a free to play game for phones and computers made with the Chinese company NetEase. It was a new idea for the franchise, and while many players loved having Diablo in their pocket, others criticised its spending options. These two releases show the two sides of the franchise today: honouring its classic roots, and trying to reach new people in new places.

sections.heading: Diablo IV
sections.script: Diablo four came out in June twenty twenty three, taking the series back to a darker and more serious tone. It has a huge shared open world, with other players visible in towns and on the map, and a story about Lilith, the daughter of Mephisto. Blizzard said it earned more than six hundred sixty six million dollars in its first five days, calling it the fastest selling game in its history. Notice that the company did not give a unit count. The game runs on seasons, with new stories and rewards every few months. It was also a step toward the series' roots, with creepy dungeons and a gritty look that brought back many longtime fans.

sections.heading: Vessel of Hatred and Lord of Hatred
sections.script: Diablo four grew through two big expansions. Vessel of Hatred came out in October twenty twenty four, and was the game's first expansion, with a new region, a new story and a new class, the Spiritborn. The second expansion, Lord of Hatred, was released on April twenty eighth, twenty twenty six, for Windows computers, PlayStation five and Xbox Series consoles. It brought back the Paladin class, adds a campaign against Mephisto in the region of Skovos, and revamps the endgame and crafting. Critics gave it generally favourable reviews. The expansions show that Blizzard is committed to the long game, giving players new reasons to return, season after season, class after class.

sections.heading: The legacy of Diablo
sections.script: Looking back, Diablo's history reads like a campaign through hell. A small team started with an experiment in randomly generated dungeons, and over the years the franchise has given us a new way of thinking about loot, classes and online co op. It also taught the industry about the costs of launches, both good and bad. The series changed through remasters, mobile games and seasons, and yet the core remains the same: kill monsters, find treasure, and become stronger. Now we want to hear from you. Which Diablo game is your favourite, and which class do you always pick first? Let us know in the comments, and subscribe for more franchise histories. Thank you for watching, and stay awhile and listen.
